market_holds: Spot $36.90 (sealed baseline, 2026-11-09 18:10 UTC), -28.3% over 20 sessions, -72% from the 52-week high and ~22% above the 52-week low; 20d realised vol 112%. Front-week (11-13) straddle 14.7%, event-implied move 11.3%, skew +2 vol points (balanced), put/call OI 0.64. Consensus Q3 revenue ~$44.5M (Zacks/Earnings Whispers, 11-02) to ~$47.2M (Chartmill), loss ~$0.41/sh, whisper loss $0.48; Chartmill shows next-quarter revenue estimates down ~5.7% over three months. FY26 consensus revenue ~$167.5M (TIKR, 11-06) against a guide of $150-200M held for three reports; H1 was $46.2M, so the low end needs ~$59M in Q4 after a $44.5M Q3. Management guided Q3 capex $350-425M and opex ~$100M/qtr, and said H2 revenue is Q4-weighted. Constellation target already slipped to ~45 BlueBirds by early 2027 (from 45-60 by end-2026); BlueBirds 14-16 have sat at the Cape since ~September with no announced launch date; New Glenn only returns in December after its May pad explosion. The October slide is tied to dated news: B. Riley downgrade 10-02, Piper downgrade, FCC approval of SpaceX's 15,000-satellite direct-to-cell system plus its ~$8B spectrum buy 10-09, a -10.5% session 10-14 to $42. Then -15% on 11-05 in a Nasdaq/AI rout and +7% on 11-06 on the Blacklift rocket/Firefly engine deal (>$1.3B, ~$900M cash plus 10-14M shares), with the rocket's unveiling on 11-12, outside the window. Short interest 64.8M shares at 9-30 (~20% of float in late-summer readings); retail sentiment on Stocktwits turned bearish in early November. A securities class action over capital and liquidity disclosures has a lead-plaintiff deadline of 11-13.
view: This is a business-update print where the reported numbers have rarely set the reaction. Revenue missed consensus in Q3 2025, Q1 2026 and Q2 2026, yet the Q2 reaction was +4.2%. The largest moves in the reaction history (-17% on 2026-07-15, likely -15% on 2026-02-11) came with financing announcements rather than results. So the lines that matter tonight are three: (1) whether the FY26 $150-200M revenue guide is held, cut, or narrowed to the bottom; (2) the launch manifest, meaning a date for BlueBirds 14-16 and how many New Glenn flights land before early 2027, which decides whether the 45-satellite target slips again; (3) how the ~$900M cash for Blacklift and the ~$3B burn through 2028 get funded, including any new convert or ATM. On (1), the Q3 consensus jump to $44.5M from $31.5M sits awkwardly with management's own statement that H2 is Q4-weighted, so a Q3 revenue miss is likely. But the market has learned to look through revenue misses, and the 5.7% cut in estimates shows some of that is already in. On (2), a further slip looks likely: no launch date for 14-16 after two months at the Cape, New Glenn not back until December, and an outside satcom consultant putting 60 satellites in 2028. But the stock is already 72% off its high on exactly this narrative, and two downgrades cite it. On (3), a raise announced with the release is the scenario that has produced -15 to -17% before. At $36.90, near a 16-month low, it is less likely than in July, and the company can point to $3.7B of pro forma cash. Against all this sit a crowded short (~20% of float), deeply bearish sentiment, a CEO who uses these calls to promote (the Blacklift event 11-12 gives him a stage), a change-of-control severance policy adopted 9-25 that has fed takeover talk, and possible upside items (a launch date, a J-LEO/Rakuten award, Ligado closing, new carrier deals). Each direction has a credible path and I could not find dated evidence the price clearly lacks. Slightly more ways for this release to disappoint than to surprise, but no edge worth a call.

recommendation.reason: The likely bad news (a Q3 revenue miss against a Q4-weighted guide, a further constellation slip, Blacklift funding questions) is real but mostly visible. Revisions, two downgrades, a 72% drawdown and bearish sentiment show the market already prices much of it. A ~20% short position and a promotional management raise the odds of a squeeze on any launch-date or contract news. I cannot show a dated fact the price misses, so no recommendation.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: A financing announcement (convert or ATM) with the release, or an FY26 revenue guide cut below $150M, would make a sharp down-gap at the open likely. A confirmed near-term launch date for BlueBirds 14-16 plus a reaffirmed guide would favour a squeeze up.

self_critique: The case for down is stronger than 46 implies. Q3 consensus assumes a 41% sequential jump that management's own Q4-weighting comment argues against. The 45-satellite target almost has to slip again given no launches since August. Blacklift adds ~$900M of cash needs that the call must explain, and this company has raised capital around results before, with -15 to -17% reactions. The case for up: the stock is at a 16-month low with ~20% short interest, and the last results reaction (+4.2% in August) came despite a revenue miss.
approach_notes: P4 helped: I could show the launch slip and the revenue risk partly in revisions, downgrades and the drawdown, so I did not call them unpriced. P6 (find the line) mattered most, because headline revenue has not driven this stock's reactions, financing and launch news have. The baseline's reaction history mixes financing 8-Ks with earnings, and separating them took effort.
